articles.headline: Lugo fijará por ordenanza una distancia mínima de tres kilómetros entre el biogás y las viviendas
articles.subtitle: El gobierno local de Elena Candia modificará el artículo 80 de la ordenanza de protección ambiental para cuantificar la separación de las industrias molestas, una medida sin referente en la normativa estatal ni autonómica.
articles.body:
El gobierno local de Lugo modificará el artículo 80 de la ordenanza municipal reguladora de protección ambiental para establecer una distancia mínima de tres kilómetros entre industrias potencialmente contaminantes, como las plantas de biogás, y los núcleos de población o las viviendas unifamiliares. La alcaldesa, Elena Candia, presentó la medida este lunes y anunció que la llevará al pleno de este mes.

La redacción actual obliga a situar "a una distancia adecuada del núcleo poblacional" las actividades "que originen excrementos de animales o produzcan residuos malolientes". El texto propuesto mantiene esa fórmula y añade que "las plantas de biogás situadas en suelo rústico deberán ubicarse a una distancia no inferior a 3.000 metros del núcleo de población más cercano". La ordenanza se publicó en el BOP el 19 de junio.

Candia subrayó que la iniciativa es pionera porque ni el Estado ni la Xunta establecen una distancia de seguridad para estas actividades, y recordó que ya era una demanda de los populares cuando estaban en la oposición. "O que xeraba a polémica sempre era a ubicación", dijo, y añadió que también pesa el tránsito de vehículos que gestionan los residuos.

Los servicios jurídicos del Concello han advertido de que modificar ese artículo obligará además a retocar alguna ordenanza del plan general. La norma llega con varios proyectos en tramitación y con plataformas vecinales movilizadas en Palas de Rei, Antas de Ulla y la comarca de A Ulloa, y también en O Saviñao, en plena Ribeira Sacra, donde la candidatura a patrimonio mundial añade presión al debate.

articles.headline: María Olga Serrano toma posesión como primera fiscala jefa de Lugo
articles.subtitle: La hasta ahora fiscal delegada de delitos de odio en A Coruña sustituye a Roberto Brezmes al frente de la Fiscalía Provincial en un acto presidido por la fiscal superior de Galicia, Carmen Eiró.
articles.body:
María Olga Serrano Pedrós toma posesión este martes como fiscala jefa de la Fiscalía Provincial de Lugo. Es la primera mujer que ocupa el cargo, que recoge de Roberto Brezmes tras una década al frente del ministerio público lucense. El acto se celebra a las 12.30 horas en la Audiencia Provincial, presidido por la fiscala superior de Galicia, Carmen Eiró, con asistencia de fiscales jefes y magistrados.

Serrano Pedrós desarrolló casi toda su carrera en la Fiscalía Provincial de A Coruña, donde era fiscal delegada de delitos de odio desde 2009. Ejerció la acusación pública en procesos de gran repercusión, como el asesinato de Samuel Luiz, el crimen de Yoel Quispe y el caso del lotero de A Coruña por la apropiación indebida de un boleto de La Primitiva premiado con 4,7 millones de euros.

Su nombramiento, a propuesta de la fiscala general del Estado, Teresa Peramato, se conoció a mediados de julio e incluyó el plan de actuación que presentó para la nueva etapa: atención a las víctimas y a las personas vulnerables, impulso de la especialización, uso de nuevas tecnologías, cooperación con otros operadores jurídicos y sociales y transparencia.

Con su incorporación, la justicia en Lugo queda dirigida por cuatro mujeres. Sandra Piñeiro preside la Audiencia Provincial; María del Carmen Varela es la secretaria coordinadora provincial de los letrados de la administración de Justicia, y Olalla Díaz, decana de los jueces de la capital, preside el Tribunal de Instancia.

articles.headline: La vieja estación de Lugo espera un uso a las puertas de la intermodal
articles.subtitle: La estación actual, la antigua casa del guarda y una nave de almacenamiento abandonada siguen sin destino definido, y vecinos y Esquerda Unida advierten del deterioro cuando se acerca la apertura de la nueva terminal.
articles.body:
Las antiguas instalaciones ferroviarias de Lugo han quedado en el limbo a medida que se acerca la puesta en marcha de la nueva estación intermodal. El entorno de la vieja estación, que durante años formó parte de la vida cotidiana del barrio, presenta una imagen que los residentes consideran poco adecuada para una zona llamada a transformarse en profundidad.

Entre las instalaciones sin uso definido están la actual estación de tren, la antigua casa del guarda y una nave de almacenamiento abandonada. Los vecinos reclaman que se concrete qué ocurrirá con esos espacios y que se evite que las dependencias ferroviarias sigan deteriorándose.

A esa preocupación se suma Esquerda Unida, que advierte de que, a las puertas de la inauguración de la intermodal, todavía no se sabe qué uso tendrán los tres edificios y considera que existe el riesgo de que queden sin utilidad por falta de planificación. EU recuerda que siempre defendió que la nueva estación aprovechase los edificios de la antigua, incluido el de Correos, finalmente derribado, en lugar de construir una terminal nueva, y culpa al Concello de la situación.

El estado de las instalaciones no es el único frente abierto: el PP y el BNG mantienen la presión sobre el Gobierno central por el desarrollo de la intermodal y la conexión ferroviaria con Santiago.

articles.headline: Sánchez fija el final del año como horizonte para Ceuta y el CIS constata un 82% partidario de reforzar la frontera
articles.subtitle: El presidente da por resuelta la situación en los próximos meses mientras Vivas le acusa de sumisión a Rabat y el barómetro del CIS evita preguntar por la gestión del Gobierno.
articles.body:
El Gobierno ha fijado por primera vez un horizonte temporal para la crisis de Ceuta. En una entrevista en La Sexta, Pedro Sánchez aseguró que espera que los trámites administrativos y el retorno de la mayoría de los migrantes estén resueltos antes de que acabe el año: "Nos hemos dado de aquí al final del año para arreglar la situación".

El presidente cifró en unos 200 los migrantes que regresan a Marruecos cada día y en 10.000 las plazas de acogida activas que aspira a tener.

Sánchez negó que el Gobierno tuviera información suficiente antes del 30 de julio para anticipar la magnitud de la entrada y tildó de "bulo" la idea de que teme a Marruecos por el espionaje con Pegasus, defendiendo una buena relación con Rabat como vía para el retorno.

La publicación del barómetro del CIS añadió munición al debate. El 82,2% de los encuestados considera necesario reforzar las fronteras de Ceuta y Melilla y el 97,1% dice estar informado de lo ocurrido, pero el sondeo no incluye ninguna pregunta sobre la gestión del Ejecutivo. El presidente ceutí, Juan Vivas, acusó al Gobierno de "irresponsabilidad" y de no querer "molestar" a Marruecos, y reprochó a Sánchez su "extraordinaria sumisión" a Rabat.

articles.headline: La Junta Electoral se parte por la mitad por la ley de nietos y evita el pulso con el Supremo
articles.subtitle: Seis vocales querían recurrir la suspensión cautelar del voto de los nacionalizados y siete lo impidieron, en la reunión más tensa del órgano desde 2020.
articles.body:
La Junta Electoral Central acordó este lunes acatar la decisión del Tribunal Supremo que suspende de forma cautelar el derecho al voto de las personas nacionalizadas al amparo de la llamada ley de nietos, pero lo hizo dividida y tras una discusión que fuentes del órgano describen como la más tensa desde enero de 2020.

Seis vocales votaron a favor de interponer un recurso de reposición para mostrar su disconformidad con el alto tribunal y siete se opusieron, según El Mundo; la propuesta decayó por la mínima.

En paralelo, cuatro vocales de orientación conservadora plantearon dar instrucciones propias para notificar individualmente la decisión a los afectados, una vía que fue rechazada por ocho votos frente a cinco. Otros miembros venían a "arreglar el desaguisado". Según elDiario.es, algunos pasajes del borrador de los letrados se suprimieron para que el acuerdo fuese lo más escueto posible.

La JEC ha encargado informes a la Oficina del Censo Electoral y a los registros consulares, a los que el Supremo pide certificar el vínculo con el exilio de quienes obtuvieron o tramitan la nacionalidad por esta vía. La suspensión llegó tras los recursos de Vox y Iustitia Europa y afecta ya a las inscripciones en el censo de residentes ausentes.

articles.headline: Feijóo prepara una ley para retirar la nacionalidad a los inmigrantes que cometan delitos graves
articles.subtitle: El PP ultima una proposición de ley orgánica que saca la nacionalidad del Código Civil, endurece el examen de idioma y valores y fija desde el primer momento los supuestos de pérdida del pasaporte.
articles.body:
El Partido Popular trabaja en una proposición de ley orgánica para endurecer el acceso a la nacionalidad española que, si llega a aprobarse, abriría la puerta a retirar el pasaporte a quienes cometan delitos graves después de haberlo obtenido.

Según adelantó El Mundo, la norma afectaría a condenados por asesinatos con agravantes, terrorismo, crimen organizado o reincidentes en agresiones sexuales. Las fuentes de Génova consultadas aseguran que esos supuestos se conocerán "desde el primer instante en el que se otorgue el pasaporte", porque se incorporarán al procedimiento de adquisición.

El texto, que el partido presenta como un paso más de su política migratoria, sacaría la nacionalidad del Código Civil y la llevaría a una ley orgánica con exigencias mayores de idioma y de "inclusión positiva" en los valores constitucionales. "La nacionalidad no se regala, la nacionalidad se merece", resumen en la dirección popular, que insiste en que la ciudadanía "no es un trámite administrativo".

No es una idea nueva en el discurso de Alberto Núñez Feijóo. En octubre de 2025 ya propuso elevar los requisitos lingüísticos, culturales y constitucionales con esa misma fórmula, y en julio de ese año planteó facilitar la expulsión de inmigrantes con residencia legal que delincan, un debate que en la práctica ya cubre el artículo 89 del Código Penal.

articles.headline: Ceuta suma 4.300 plazas ocupadas mientras el Trampolín crece sin freno y el agua potable queda a la vista del campamento
articles.subtitle: El Gobierno prepara un millar de plazas nuevas en el Muelle de Poniente pese a los informes técnicos que las califican de críticas, y los realojos empujan nuevos asentamientos junto a la desalinizadora.
articles.body:
El dispositivo de acogida desplegado en Ceuta tras la entrada masiva de los días 30 y 31 de julio roza ya su límite. Migraciones daba por cubiertas este lunes 4.300 plazas en centros acondicionados y afrontaba el último traslado de envergadura: más de 800 personas conduidas desde el barrio de Loma Colmenar hasta el asentamiento temporal de Los Rosales.

Con las plazas pendientes y las prometidas para el campamento de Sidi Embarek, donde viven unas 300 mujeres y niñas, el Ejecutivo ha comprometido cerca de 6.000 plazas.

La siguiente parada prevista es el Muelle de Poniente, en la zona portuaria, donde el Gobierno quiere habilitar un millar de plazas más pese a que las instalaciones están catalogadas como "críticas" en los informes técnicos, según El Mundo.

El goteo de desalojos en el monte Hacho, el Sarchal y el Morro no ha vaciado la ciudad de campamentos precarios: los ha desplazado. El asentamiento de la playa del Trampolín suma nuevos moradores y chabolas cada día, y algunos migrantes se han instalado en la playa Benítez, al otro lado de la desalinizadora que garantiza el agua potable de Ceuta, una zona que quedará inundada con la pleamar y el hacinamiento, advierten quienes viven allí.

articles.headline: O'Neill signs Cardiff declaration on self-determination as Little-Pengelly accuses her of weaponising her role
articles.subtitle: The Sinn Féin, SNP and Plaid Cymru leaders signed a joint declaration in Cardiff saying their nations' future lies in the EU, and the DUP deputy First Minister says she was neither consulted nor asked for permission.
articles.body:
Michelle O'Neill, John Swinney and Rhun ap Iorwerth signed a joint declaration in Cardiff on Monday calling for self-determination for Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The three met as party leaders rather than as heads of government, and Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald travelled with O'Neill for the summit.

The statement says Brexit "damaged our economies" and that the future of the three nations "belongs to the European Union", with the leaders pledging to rebuild European trade, investment and cultural ties. It also asserts that their nations "have the right to self-determination" and that no Westminster government has the right to block democracy, while acknowledging that each nation has different constitutional positions and will decide its own future in its own time.

Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly criticised O'Neill for attending, saying she had not sought any agreement or permission to travel, attend or sign anything as First Minister, and accused republicanism of attempting to weaponise the role of First Minister. In Northern Ireland the First and deputy First Ministers hold identical powers.

Sinn Féin's John O'Dowd said O'Neill was there as party deputy leader and that it was "right and proper" for parties favouring greater self-determination to cooperate. It is the first time since devolution that Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales have all been led by first ministers who want to leave the UK.

articles.headline: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania as Vilnius scrambles to identify its origin
articles.subtitle: The drone crossed into Lithuanian airspace from the direction of Belarus overnight, prompting phone alerts in the Vilnius region days after a similar incursion over Poland.
articles.body:
Lithuania's president, Gitanas Nausėda, said NATO fighter jets destroyed a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight, with the aircraft approaching from the direction of Belarus. The drone was brought down near Kaunas, according to the Guardian, and the national crisis management centre said it had not yet established where the drone came from.

Air-raid style alerts were issued to phones in the Vilnius region as the incident unfolded. It came as the wider region remains on edge after recent violations of NATO airspace, including Russian drones that Poland's air force, supported by allied aircraft, shot down over Polish territory, one of which damaged a house.

The confusion was compounded by Sky News, which reported that an earlier drone alert over Lithuania turned out to be a flock of birds after a NATO jet was scrambled. Lithuanian officials have repeatedly warned that the Baltic states are on the front line of Russia's pressure campaign and have asked allies to keep air-defence assets in the region permanently.

Moscow has dismissed Western complaints over drone incursions, describing its operations as aimed at targets in Ukraine, while NATO members have quietly discussed whether the alliance's eastern airspace rules need tightening.

articles.headline: Supreme Court refuses to let the Postal Service enforce its new mail-voting rule before the midterms
articles.subtitle: The justices left in place a nationwide injunction, with Kavanaugh saying states have no time to adapt and Alito, joined by Thomas, dissenting in a decision taken with ballots already in the post.
articles.body:
The US Supreme Court on Monday night declined to lift a lower-court ruling that bars the United States Postal Service from enforcing new regulations for mail-in ballots, handing the Trump administration a defeat less than two months before the November midterm elections.

In a brief unsigned order, the court said the government "is unlikely to succeed on the merits of its challenge" to the preliminary injunction issued by District Judge Indira Talwani in Boston, and that the equitable factors did not favour an emergency stay.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh concurred, writing that there is "at least a fair prospect" that the final rule falls within the Postal Service's statutory authority, but that applying it this year "would be arbitrary and capricious" because state and local officials lack time to implement it.

Justice Samuel Alito, joined by Clarence Thomas, dissented, arguing the plaintiffs lacked standing and that the Postal Service has broad power to regulate the mail.

The rule, finalised in late August to implement a March executive order from President Donald Trump, would have required ballot envelopes to carry an election-mail logo and a per-voter barcode, and states to upload voter information to a Postal Service portal. Mail ballots account for nearly a third of votes cast in the United States, and ballots are already going out in North Carolina and Alabama.

articles.headline: Two Houthi strikes set Saudi oil tankers ablaze at a Red Sea terminal and rattle crude markets
articles.subtitle: The attacks on vessels off Yanbu came within 24 hours of each other, hitting the port that ships crude from the kingdom's east-west pipeline, and shipping traffic through Bab al-Mandeb has collapsed.
articles.body:
Two attacks in as many days by Yemen's Houthi movement have set oil tankers ablaze off the Saudi Arabian coast, striking vessels connected to the Red Sea terminal of Yanbu, roughly 150 miles north of Jeddah. The first missile hit on Saturday and a second tanker was attacked on Sunday, with no injuries reported, according to RTÉ.

The New York Times reported that the strikes hit ships associated with the Muxtar Babayev and Motaro, and that the attacks had not yet imperilled oil flows outright, even as the Yemeni government demanded a decisive international response. Yanbu is the western terminus of the pipeline that carries Saudi crude from the Gulf to the Red Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have said their campaign is a response to Israeli operations in Gaza and that their forces will continue targeting shipping they associate with Israel and its allies. Saudi officials have struck a cautious tone, aware that a full campaign against the group risks another cycle of direct confrontation, as happened when the port of Hodeidah was devastated in 2024. Traffic through the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a chokepoint for Europe-Asia trade, remains far below its historic levels.

articles.headline: EPA scraps limits on greenhouse gases from power plants and proposes ending all remaining rules
articles.subtitle: Announcing a final repeal and a sweeping new proposal in Houston, administrator Lee Zeldin said coal production for electricity could rise more than tenfold, and legal challenges are expected.
articles.body:
The Trump administration is repealing greenhouse gas limits on the country's fossil fuel-fired power plants, the EPA announced on Monday, in what administrator Lee Zeldin described as the largest deregulatory action on the US power sector in history.

Speaking in Houston at a G20 energy summit, Zeldin said the agency was finalising the repeal of most of the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards, which required existing coal plants and new gas plants to cut carbon dioxide emissions from the 2030s, including 90% carbon capture requirements.

In a separate proposal, the EPA said it wants to rescind every remaining greenhouse gas standard for power plants, arguing that the Clean Air Act does not give it the authority to regulate emissions in response to climate change. The agency puts the savings from the repeal at more than $300bn and says coal use in power generation could increase by more than ten times.

The legal reasoning rests on the February rescission of the 2009 endangerment finding and on the 2024 Loper Bright decision, and builds on the earlier repeal of vehicle emissions standards. Environmental lawyers expect the rules to be challenged immediately. The proposal will be open to a 45-day public comment period.

articles.headline: Sweden's election hangs on a single seat as the far-right loses ground
articles.subtitle: Preliminary results give the left-wing bloc a one-seat advantage in the Riksdag, with the Sweden Democrats slipping and postal votes from abroad still to be counted.
articles.body:
Sweden's general election is too close to call after preliminary results gave the left-wing bloc a one-seat advantage over the centre-right in the Riksdag, according to projections reported by Sky News. The far-right Sweden Democrats, the party that has reshaped Swedish politics over the past decade, lost ground compared with its previous showing.

Al Jazeera reported that the race remained open, with the outcome dependent on late-counted postal and overseas ballots. Under Sweden's proportional system, a handful of seats can determine which bloc is given the mandate to form a government, and both the Social Democrats and the conservative Moderate party have ruled out governing with the Sweden Democrats' support.

The Spanish daily ABC highlighted the role of voters with immigrant backgrounds, arguing that naturalised Swedes — including a large Latin American community — had helped tilt the balance towards the left. Sweden's election authority has not yet published a definitive result, and party leaders are expected to begin exploratory talks in the coming days, with the question of who can assemble a working majority still unresolved.

articles.headline: Apple ships iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate 27 with a rebuilt Siri — and a waitlist to use it
articles.subtitle: The annual updates arrive with an LLM-powered assistant, an opacity slider for Liquid Glass, and the last macOS release that will run Intel apps through Rosetta.
articles.body:
Apple released its 2026 operating system updates on Monday: iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, watchOS 27, visionOS 27 and tvOS 27.

The flagship feature is Siri AI, a large language model-based overhaul of the assistant that can answer questions about what is on screen, search a user's past emails and messages, and act inside third-party apps that have adopted Apple's interfaces. There is also a standalone Siri app, and Apple now lets users generate Shortcuts automations and Safari extensions from a prompt.

Access is not universal. Siri AI runs on Apple's own AFM 3 family of models, from a 3-billion-parameter on-device model to larger cloud models, and requires an iPhone 15 Pro or an iPhone 16 or later with the device language set to English. Apple is rolling the feature out through a waitlist: users install iOS 27, open Settings, choose Siri and tap "Try Siri AI (beta)".

iOS 27 runs on iPhone 11 and later, but Golden Gate needs an M-series Mac and is the final macOS release to support Rosetta for Intel apps, with an exception carved out for older Intel-era games. Liquid Glass also gets a slider controlling how transparent or opaque the interface looks.

articles.headline: Musk's X and SpaceXAI drop Apple from their antitrust suit but keep fighting OpenAI
articles.subtitle: The companies filed to dismiss their claims against Apple with prejudice, leaving the case against OpenAI to continue as a would-be successor to Musk's earlier lawsuit.
articles.body:
X and SpaceXAI, the artificial intelligence company formerly known as xAI, have moved to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple in the antitrust lawsuit they filed over Apple's integration of ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence.

In the filing, the plaintiffs say they have "resolved their claims" against Apple and are moving under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 41(a)(2) to dismiss them with prejudice, a step Apple does not oppose. Critically, they explicitly state they are not dropping any claims against the OpenAI entities. Judge Mark Pittman still has to approve the dismissal.

The lawsuit dates to last year, when Elon Musk accused Apple and OpenAI of colluding to keep competing AI apps from gaining visibility on the App Store, arguing that the ChatGPT deal gave OpenAI an unfair advantage. Both companies denied the claims and the case moved into discovery, including a fight that ended with a judge ordering Musk to hand over potentially relevant emails from his Tesla and SpaceX accounts.

The remaining OpenAI action resembles a spiritual successor to Musk's separate suit against OpenAI, Sam Altman, Greg Brockman and Microsoft, which collapsed in May when a jury found the claims had been filed too late.

articles.headline: ClickFix attacks turn fake CAPTCHAs into malware installs on Macs and Windows PCs
articles.subtitle: Attackers are hijacking legitimate accounts and websites to serve prompts that persuade users to paste a command into Terminal or PowerShell, handing over passwords and crypto wallets.
articles.body:
A social-engineering technique known as ClickFix has grown from a curiosity into one of the most effective malware delivery methods of the year, and it now targets both Windows and macOS.

The lure is a fake CAPTCHA or anti-bot check, often injected into a legitimate website or into an advertisement. When the user clicks, they are told to "verify" by copying a line of text and pasting it into Windows' Run dialog or PowerShell, or into the Terminal on a Mac.

Pressing return installs an information stealer that immediately begins harvesting passwords, logged-in accounts and crypto wallets. Because the payload runs in a shell with the user's own privileges, it often slips past antivirus tools.

The latest campaign involved the official HBO Max account on Reddit, which attackers compromised to post hundreds of fake but convincing adverts linking to a page that imitates the streaming service and serves a ClickFix lure, according to Hudson Rock and a thread in Reddit's cybersecurity community.

Security researcher Kevin Beaumont has noted that organisations can blunt the technique by blocking shell access for ordinary users, while Mac users can run tools such as BlockBlock. Researchers warn that state-sponsored groups have adopted the method too.

articles.headline: Apple's update day doubles as a mass security patch, fixing 200-plus vulnerabilities
articles.subtitle: Alongside the new features, macOS Golden Gate 27, Tahoe 26.7 and Sequoia 15.8 close hundreds of holes, and iOS 27 arrives with its own lengthy list of security fixes.
articles.body:
Apple's operating system release is also one of its largest security patch drops of the year. According to 9to5Mac, macOS 27 Golden Gate along with the maintenance updates macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8 fix more than 200 vulnerabilities, covering users who cannot or do not wish to move to the newest major version.

iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 ship with their own set of security fixes, catalogued in Apple's release notes. MacRumors has separately published a list of the bugs addressed in iOS 27, including crashes and interface glitches that users have reported over the past year.

The volume of fixes underlines how much of the annual release cycle is defensive work rather than feature work — and how quickly the window between a patch and public exploitation has shrunk for unpatched devices. Security researchers have repeatedly urged users to install the updates promptly, since the details of the flaws become public in Apple's advisories as soon as the fixes ship, giving attackers a map for anyone who delays.

Apple has not disclosed any indication that the vulnerabilities were being exploited in the wild before the release.

articles.headline: Trump calls talk of slowing AI a 'hoax' as Nvidia's chief takes his call on stage — and AI stocks slide
articles.subtitle: Jensen Huang put the US president on speaker mid-panel after Anthropic's Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow down, while investors trimmed their exposure to the AI trade.
articles.body:
The fight over how fast to build artificial intelligence spilled into the open on Monday. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, appearing at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles, took a phone call from President Donald Trump on stage and put him on speaker for the audience.

Trump used the moment to attack those urging restraint. "They're just playing right in the hands of a lot of people that don't want to see it happen," he said, according to TechCrunch. "That could be political people. It could also be China. And we're not going to let that happen. It's a hoax." Huang replied: "You're right.

We're not going to let that happen, sir." The exchange followed a weekend intervention by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who called for slowing the pace at which AI capabilities are improved — a position Elon Musk and Sam Altman have also publicly endorsed, while Huang has taken the opposite view.

Trump later said he was "with you all the way" and that the United States would lead, while acknowledging the industry should proceed "prudently". The Guardian reported that the same doubts that prompted Amodei's intervention were also visible in the market, with AI-linked shares sliding as investors questioned how quickly the enormous spending on models and data centres will translate into profits.

articles.headline: OpenAI quietly buys Glass Imaging, a startup chasing DSLR-quality photos from tiny phone cameras
articles.subtitle: The Wall Street Journal reports a deal worth more than $300 million for a Los Altos company founded by former Apple imaging engineers, a big jump from its roughly $100 million valuation last year.
articles.body:
OpenAI has acquired Glass Imaging, a startup developing artificial intelligence that improves the quality of images captured by the small sensors in smartphones, in a deal reported by the Wall Street Journal and valued at more than $300 million.

Glass Imaging was founded in 2019 and is based in Los Altos, California. Its team includes former Apple imaging engineers, and Calcalist notes it was founded by an Israeli entrepreneur, giving OpenAI both hardware-oriented expertise and a presence in Israel's imaging talent pool. The company had raised about $30 million before the acquisition and was valued at roughly $100 million in a funding round last year, making the reported price a significant step up.

The technology aims to match the output of a dedicated DSLR camera using computational photography and AI processing rather than larger optics — the same physics-defying pitch that has driven much of the improvement in phone cameras over the past decade.

OpenAI has not said how it intends to use the technology, though it is assembling a hardware business around its acquisition of Jony Ive's design venture and a growing line of consumer devices. SiliconANGLE noted the purchase adds to a pattern of OpenAI buying small technical teams rather than announcing splashy acquisitions.

articles.headline: The AI power crunch: agentic tools are driving a data centre boom the grid cannot keep up with
articles.subtitle: Gartner expects global data centre demand to hit 132 GW this year and 290 GW by 2030, while developers install gas turbines and repurpose old factories rather than wait for new transmission lines.
articles.body:
The reason so many data centres are being built is not the chatbot query, according to Wired's Power Play column: it is the shift to AI agents. Rather than answering one question, agents give themselves hundreds of smaller prompts, re-prompting themselves dozens of times to complete a task — a far more compute-hungry way of using models, and one that is now driving the buildout. Many developers are not waiting for the grid either, installing gas turbines on site.

The numbers behind the crunch are stark. The Register reports that Gartner expects worldwide data centre power demand to reach 132 GW in 2026, up from 104 GW in 2025, and 290 GW by 2030, while Morgan Stanley projects US demand could reach 74 GW by 2028 against a shortfall of roughly 49 GW.

The infrastructure firm Teravolt forecasts demand of 410 GW by 2036 against 170 GW of available grid power, noting that data centres can be built in one to three years while new grid infrastructure takes five to 15.

Teravolt's answer is to cannibalise older industries — repurposing former aluminium smelters, refineries, bitcoin farms and thermal plants, chiefly in Eastern and Southern Europe, where brownfield sites remain cheap and customers demanding 20,000 GPUs within a year can be served. Meanwhile the Federation of American Scientists has told local officials to negotiate harder, warning that tax abatements can cost states more than $1 billion a year and that decommissioning terms are largely untested.
